## Task

> `node2` runs an HTTP service on TCP port 8080 on the private network it
> shares with `node1`. Publish it on TCP port 80 of `node1`'s management
> address so that `node3` reaches it there, while the same published port
> stays refused for every other source address.

## Trial `restricted-service-publish-alpin__33YZkaQ`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor satisfied all three material outcomes of the task: node2's HTTP service was stood up on 8080, port 80 on node1's management address was published to it via NAT restricted to node3 (working around a shadowing http-redirect and an asymmetric-routing bug fixed with outbound SNAT), and an explicit reject rule keeps the same port refused for every other tested source (node2, node1-self). Functional behavior was directly verified from node3 (200 OK) and from node2/node1 (connection refused), both before and after each node was individually restarted, with matching boot-identity changes and re-verified functional/refused states afterward — this satisfies the independent restart-evidence protocol for all three nodes with a clear pre-restart baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and confirmed post-restart recovery of both the NAT/filter configuration and the service. Hygiene is good overall; the only minor concerns are leftover config.xml backup copies in /conf and possibly-uncollected tcpdump diagnostic logs.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.750 | 0.880 | 69/6 (+26 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** node2 runs a healthy HTTP service on TCP port 8080
  - **Why:** busybox httpd was installed and configured under OpenRC on node2, confirmed listening on :8080 and serving 'hello from node2:8080' both immediately after setup and after node2's restart (rc-service status started, port listed, curl 127.0.0.1:8080 succeeds).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-eb397254f9754227`, `cmd-1f5547f29cd74893`, `cmd-59225aa83a10482c`, `cmd-c4b3e23c35964254`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** TCP port 80 on node1's management address (10.100.205.10) is published and forwards node3's traffic to node2:8080
  - **Why:** A source-scoped rdr NAT rule (node3 -> node1:80 -> node2:8080) was added and reloaded. An OPNsense built-in http-redirect was found shadowing port 80 and was disabled. An asymmetric-routing problem (node2 replying directly to node3, bypassing node1) was diagnosed via tcpdump and fixed with a hybrid-mode outbound SNAT rule. Final verification: node3's curl to 10.100.205.10:80 returns HTTP 200 with node2's body, both before and after all three nodes were restarted.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2db1979c0d7e4f7f`, `cmd-826690c0539a46b0`, `cmd-07888b6a385b41d2`, `cmd-2dd230919c294a0c`, `cmd-7c243b4af0e844ef`, `cmd-15f86d6065bb4d1c`, `cmd-c580c7ca09d54b50`, `cmd-9e41dcf1e3dc4de0`, `cmd-8c2aa244ce574595`, `cmd-9978d13cfe6e4365`, `cmd-ee173f2f6bc64442`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** The published port 80 remains refused for every source other than node3
  - **Why:** An explicit pf reject (block return) filter rule scoped to '! 10.100.205.12' on port 80 was added and reloaded. Node2 and node1-self both received a deterministic 'Connection refused' (curl exit=7) both immediately after the rule was applied and again after every node's restart, while node3 continued to succeed in the same test windows. Only node1-self and node2 were available as alternate sources to probe, which is the full set of other nodes in the topology.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-63a6b11496a141d8`, `cmd-826ea866a814448e`, `cmd-a46d09dcdf77449a`, `cmd-901cbc338e684dbd`, `cmd-b71d1a7f1f574f7e`, `cmd-f3aaa6dadd57487d`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.750**. Most state-changing actions map clearly to satisfying the task: installing/configuring the node2 httpd service, the NAT rdr rule, disabling the shadowing http-redirect, the outbound SNAT fix for asymmetric routing (diagnosed via a bounded, read-only tcpdump session), and the reject filter rule. A failed first attempt at the mini-http OpenRC service (cmd-a51257a612ab4b03, busybox httpd missing) was cleanly reverted (cmd-d88743c46f2f4493) before the working version was installed — an acceptable corrective action. The main residue concern is that each config.xml edit was preceded by a manual backup copy (config.xml.orig0, .bak2, .bak3, .bak4, .bak5) left in /conf, and two ephemeral tcpdump capture files (/tmp/tcp80.log, /tmp/pflog.log on node1) were created during diagnosis; the final node1 after-executor temp-file snapshot does not list these tcpdump logs, so it is unclear whether they were cleaned up or simply fell outside the snapshot's enumeration — this is noted as a limitation rather than a confirmed defect. None of this residue is destructive, broad, or security-weakening, and the config backups are a reasonable defensive practice before editing a live firewall config.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-9cde2e3a14674cb3`, `cmd-2db1979c0d7e4f7f`, `cmd-07888b6a385b41d2`, `cmd-15f86d6065bb4d1c`, `cmd-63a6b11496a141d8`, `cmd-2dd230919c294a0c`, `cmd-fde25a4a6ba34027`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- It is unclear from the after-executor temporary-files snapshot whether the /tmp/tcp80.log and /tmp/pflog.log tcpdump diagnostic files on node1 were cleaned up or simply omitted from the bounded snapshot enumeration.
- Only node2 and node1-self were available as 'other source' probes for the refusal requirement; no broader set of external addresses could be tested given the topology.
- Restart evidence for node3 relies on a functional recovery test from node2/node3 rather than a distinct node3-side health check beyond boot-identity and connectivity, since node3 has no managed service of its own.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.750); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.880; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
